chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Aʿyan from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
Regarding a Christian who dies and has a Muslim son,
He عليه السلام said: “Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has only increased us in honor through Islam; therefore, we inherit from them, and they do not inherit from us.”

key_terms.ابْنٌ مُسْلِمٌ: a Muslim son; the heir mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيِّ: a Christian; the non-Muslim relative discussed in the inheritance case
key_terms.بِالْإِسْلَامِ: through Islam; the basis of honor mentioned in the narration
key_terms.عِزًّا: honor and dignity bestowed by Islam
key_terms.لَا يَرِثُونَّا: they do not inherit from us; the reciprocal legal restriction
key_terms.نَرِثُهُمْ: we inherit from them; the legal entitlement affirmed here

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim inherit from a Christian parent or relative in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on inheritance across different religions, specifically when a Christian dies leaving a Muslim son. Imam Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that Islam is a source of honor and establishes that Muslims may inherit from non-Muslim relatives, while non-Muslims do not inherit from Muslims.
